correctness.rationale: Actual RESULT.md defines faces as sets of vertex-disjoint directed paths, includes isolated vertices, and allows antiparallel arcs. An (n-1)-arc face is a spanning Hamiltonian path and an (n-2)-arc ridge has exactly two path components, with at most two joining arcs. Two possible completions close one unique directed Hamiltonian cycle. Paths lacking a closing arc have a private ridge so zero coefficient in any top cycle; all remaining Hamiltonian-path faces split into disjoint blocks of n facets per directed Hamiltonian cycle. In each block the integral top-boundary kernel is the primitive rank-one boundary of a formal (n-1)-simplex, and no n-arc simplices exist, proving the direct integral sum. Arc permutation signs give the precise G-module. A bidirected wheel corresponds to m omitted rim edges times two traversal orientations, free transitive D_m orbit. Independent exhaustive mod-2 top-boundary checks for all 64 n=3 and 4096 n=4 digraphs matched cycle counts, not used as proof for n>4.

value.rationale: A uniform exact primitive integral basis identifies when highest multipath homology is nonzero exactly by Hamiltonicity, and gives all graph-automorphism actions, including a natural regular dihedral module for bidirected wheels. This is structural chain information unavailable from homology-rank tables or field checks.

final_claim: For any finite loopless simple digraph on n>=3 vertices, the top possible reduced multipath homology H~_{n-2}(X(D);Z) is the free Z-module on formal boundaries of directed spanning Hamiltonian cycles, with signed permutation action by graph automorphisms; for a bidirected m-rim wheel, m>=4, this module is Z[D_m].
limitations: Only top possible reduced degree is determined, with no lower homology or fast Hamiltonicity algorithm.
The n<=4 exhaustive finite computation validates only those cases, while the ridge-block proof carries the full quantifier.
